short_bio: Songwriter who received the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature.
biography:
Bob Dylan was born Robert Allen Zimmerman in Duluth, Minnesota, in 1941 and moved to New York City in 1961. His second album, The Freewheelin’ Bob Dylan (1963), carried songs that became anthems of the civil rights era.

In 1965 he moved to electric instruments with Bringing It All Back Home and Highway 61 Revisited, and his amplified set at that year’s Newport Folk Festival divided the audience. A motorcycle accident in 1966 interrupted his touring. Blood on the Tracks followed in 1975.

The Swedish Academy gave him the 2016 Nobel Prize in Literature, the first time the prize went to a songwriter, for the poetry he had brought to American song. He received the Presidential Medal of Freedom in 2012.
